question: Which statement best describes the fundamental definition of a computer network?
options: A group of connected devices that exchange data and share resources
A single standalone computer operating offline without cables
A software program used strictly for editing text documents
A collection of monitors connected to a single power outlet
answer: A group of connected devices that exchange data and share resources

question: In data communications, what term refers to the formal set of rules governing how devices exchange information?
Which capability represents a core communication benefit enabled by modern computer networks?
options: Sending messages, emails, video calls, and web access
Increasing the physical voltage of electrical outlets
Erasing unwanted files automatically from hard drives
answer: Sending messages, emails, video calls, and web access

question: Which peripheral hardware device is most frequently shared across a networked office or university lab?
Which interactive simulation software developed by Cisco allows students to design network topologies and analyze packet flow?
What does the networking abbreviation 'PAN' officially stand for?

What does the networking acronym 'LAN' represent?
A localized computer setup spanning a single room, lab, or office floor is categorized as a:
Which network scope is engineered to provide connectivity across an entire town or municipality?
Which classification applies to a large-scale network spanning across regions, countries, or international borders?
The worldwide Internet operates as the largest and most prominent real-world example of a:
In which physical network topology does every endpoint connect directly back to a central switch?
Which network layout connects all participating devices in line along a single shared backbone cable?
Which topology incorporates redundant point-to-point connections so data can be rerouted if any single link goes down?
When an organization blends two or more distinct topological architectures into a single network, it is called a:
Which hardware unit combats signal attenuation by receiving, cleaning, and amplifying signals over extended cabling distances?
Which legacy networking device operates as a simple multiport repeater, broadcasting all incoming frames out to every port?
Which device is designed to divide or join two distinct LAN segments and filter traffic based on MAC addresses?
Which modern LAN device builds a MAC address table to intelligently forward Ethernet frames exclusively to the intended recipient?
Which layer-3 device examines IP packet headers to route traffic between disparate logical subnets or networks?
Which fundamental statement accurately distinguishes the operational roles of a switch versus a router?
options: A switch connects devices within a LAN; a router connects different networks
A router connects devices within a LAN; a switch connects different networks
A hub connects devices within a LAN; a repeater connects different networks
A bridge connects devices within a LAN; a switch connects different networks
answer: A switch connects devices within a LAN; a router connects different networks

question: Which dedicated security mechanism inspects incoming and outgoing network traffic and enforces allow/deny policies?
How many distinct hierarchical layers make up the standard OSI reference model?
Which uppermost OSI layer (Layer 7) provides network interfaces and communication services directly to end-user software?
Which fundamental layer of the OSI model (Layer 1) manages unstructured bitstreams across physical copper, fiber, or wireless media?
Which OSI layer (Layer 2) packages raw bits into structured frames and handles node-to-node delivery via MAC addresses?
Which layer of the OSI model (Layer 3) is responsible for logical IP addressing, path determination, and packet forwarding?
Which OSI layer (Layer 4) oversees host-to-host segment delivery, flow control, and multiplexing using TCP or UDP?
Which OSI layer (Layer 6) acts as a data translator, handling data syntax formatting, character encoding, encryption, and compression?
What fundamental role does an IP (Internet Protocol) address fulfill in a computer network?
options: Uniquely identifying a device logically on a network for routing data
Measuring the physical temperature of the CPU
Storing operating system files permanently on the hard drive
Providing physical electric power to the network card
answer: Uniquely identifying a device logically on a network for routing data

question: How do IPv4 and IPv6 addresses differ with respect to their total bit lengths?
options: IPv4 is 32 bits, while IPv6 is 128 bits
IPv4 is 16 bits, while IPv6 is 32 bits
IPv4 is 64 bits, while IPv6 is 128 bits
IPv4 is 128 bits, while IPv6 is 256 bits
answer: IPv4 is 32 bits, while IPv6 is 128 bits

question: Which description accurately specifies what a MAC (Media Access Control) address is and its bit length?
options: A 48-bit physical hardware address permanently assigned to a NIC
A 32-bit logical address assigned dynamically by an ISP
A 128-bit security password used for Wi-Fi encryption
An 8-bit subnet mask configured on a router
answer: A 48-bit physical hardware address permanently assigned to a NIC

question: What essential mapping task does the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) perform on an IPv4 local network?
options: Resolving a known IP address to its corresponding physical MAC address
Encrypting web traffic between a browser and a server
Assigning dynamic IP addresses automatically to newly joined hosts
Translating domain names into numerical IP addresses
answer: Resolving a known IP address to its corresponding physical MAC address

question: Which network service dynamically configures client endpoints with IP addresses, subnet masks, and default gateways upon connection?
Why is the Domain Name System (DNS) commonly described as the 'phonebook of the Internet'?
options: Translating human-friendly domain names (e.g., www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses
Securing file transfers with password encryption
Assigning hardware MAC addresses to network switches
Compressing image files for faster web loading
answer: Translating human-friendly domain names (e.g., www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses

question: What primary security distinction separates standard HTTP web traffic from secure HTTPS?
options: HTTPS encrypts data transfers using SSL/TLS, whereas HTTP sends data in unencrypted plain text
HTTP is for secure banking, while HTTPS is only for public web browsing
HTTP uses port 443, while HTTPS uses port 80
HTTP is connection-oriented, while HTTPS is completely connectionless
answer: HTTPS encrypts data transfers using SSL/TLS, whereas HTTP sends data in unencrypted plain text

question: Which well-known standard TCP port numbers are assigned respectively to unencrypted HTTP and secure HTTPS communications?
options: HTTP uses port 80, and HTTPS uses port 443
HTTP uses port 21, and HTTPS uses port 22
HTTP uses port 53, and HTTPS uses port 67
HTTP uses port 25, and HTTPS uses port 110
answer: HTTP uses port 80, and HTTPS uses port 443

question: In the standard 4-layer TCP/IP protocol suite architecture, what are the four functional layers in order?
options: 4 layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, and Application
7 layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
5 layers: User, Session, Packet, Frame, and Bit
answer: 4 layers: Network Access, Internet, Transport, and Application

question: What is the key functional difference between the TCP and UDP protocols at the Transport layer?
options: TCP is reliable and connection-oriented, while UDP is faster, connectionless, and best-effort
TCP is connectionless, while UDP guarantees 100% acknowledged packet delivery
TCP operates at Layer 2, while UDP operates at Layer 7
TCP is used exclusively for video streaming, while UDP is used for web browsing
answer: TCP is reliable and connection-oriented, while UDP is faster, connectionless, and best-effort
